disease_label_per_paper: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae carrying blaOXA-48, blaVIM-2, blaCMY-2 and blaSHV-1 with septic shock and catheter-associated bacteremia
presentation_summary: 58-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes was admitted to ICU with septic shock 13 days after coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve replacement.
He was mechanically ventilated, required norepinephrine, had fever 39.5 C, and had an internal jugular central venous catheter in place for 6 days.

Cultures from catheter tip and two blood samples, including catheter and peripheral blood, grew Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to all tested antibiotics including imipenem, colistin, and tigecycline; amikacin was intermediate.
PCR detected blaOXA-48, blaVIM-2, blaCMY-2, and blaSHV-1. He improved after high-dose imipenem plus amikacin with CVVHDF and source management, and was discharged from ICU after completing therapy.
